newsitem.title: UK: Shell, Exxon name additives JV head.
newsitem.headline: Shell, Exxon name additives JV head.

text.p: Shell Group and Exxon Corp nominated Anthony J. Gaskell to become president and chief executive officer for their additives joint venture which will become effective later this year.
Gaskell was Exxon Chemical's vice president of Vistalon and Adhesives Industry.
The oil giants first announced their plan for the 50/50 worldwide petroleum additives venture in July last year. It still needs definite agreement and government approvals.
In a joint statement, Shell and Exxon said on Tuesday that their additives venture will be headquartered in Britain.
As part of the venture plan, some Shell Chemical employees are expected to move from Houston, Texas to the site of the Exxon Chemical Paramins Division in Linden, New Jersey.

The joint venture will eventually have one site in Britain. After government approval, Shell and Exxon will decide whether this will the Paramins and Development site at Abingdon, west of London, or Shell's additives research and development centre in the north west of England.
"Choosing between the sites requires an overall technology information exchange and assessment which is not possible until governmental and regulatory approvals are received," Shell and Exxon said.
Petroleum additives are used to lubricate all kind of motors and engines as well as to improve their overall operation.
